XF Studio authors complete eye-makeup presets, keeps them in a local library, previews them on V and builds a private candidate for one in-game selector. This guide defines how its interface looks and behaves, and how new work composes from the same parts. Every pattern states what it contains, when it appears, how it combines and adapts, and which application action or read-only state drives it.

Implementedin the Studio today (public/index.html)Future direction · not builtroom left in the design; needs actions and discussion firstRuleapplies to all work
01

Foundations

A restrained Cyberpunk: graphite instruments under a single signal yellow, with cyan reserved for live state. The only ornament is the bevel — a clipped corner borrowed from industrial labelling. No neon glow, glitch, scanline or fake HUD chrome: atmosphere never costs legibility. Tokens are defined once with light-dark(); a container's color-scheme chooses the theme, so every specimen below renders in either theme and in the side-by-side comparison.

Design principles

Rule
  1. Truth before polish. Never show stale, partial, unverified or preview-only results as ready, packaged or game-tested. Status words come from the application, not from the control.
  2. One accent, one meaning. Yellow marks commitment and focus (primary action, active tab, keyboard focus). Cyan marks what is live or selected. Everything else is graphite.
  3. The stage is neutral. The 3D head and UV map sit on a near-achromatic grey surround, light in the light theme and dark in the dark theme, so colour judgement isn't skewed by coloured chrome.
  4. Every affordance is an action. Buttons, menus, shortcuts, drags and the command palette call the same typed application action and show the same disabled reason.
  5. Panels are tools, not places. Any panel can dock, float, tab or join a magnetic composite; nothing depends on a fixed sidebar.
  6. Density with air. Compact 28 px controls and 32 px rows, but generous section spacing and one idea per section.
  7. Previews are diagrams. Neutral subject, one ink, one light, one frame per row; the 3D view is the true preview.
What
The rules every new screen, panel or control is reviewed against.
When
Before designing a feature and again at review. A proposal that breaks one of these needs an explicit exception recorded in the architecture boundary.
Avoid
Literal franchise tropes (glitch text, chromatic aberration, neon outlines, fake terminals), decorative animation, and colour used only for mood.

What
Semantic surfaces, lines, text and state colours. Contrast was computed for both themes: all text tokens ≥4.5:1 on panels, control boundaries (--line-strong) ≥3:1, focus ≥11:1.

Always reference a token, never a literal colour. User-authored makeup colours are content and are shown unmodified inside swatches.

Preview tokens

Implemented
--pv-groundTile ground: the stage's centre tone, flat
--pv-subjectThe neutral head, face or body
--pv-inkThe choice itself
--pv-shadeHow much shadow darkens ink and subject: a number the colour matrix reads (--pv-shade-light .72, --pv-shade-dark .62)
What
The four tokens every choice preview is coloured from (lib-choice-preview). A preview is stored as channels (feature and subject coverage, light), and one SVG colour matrix per theme (built from these tokens) turns them into colours, so a theme change needs no new picture.
When
Only for previews. A preview uses these tokens and nothing else (later: the V's own colour for the ink, when tinted).
Combine
Inside the Choice preview tile (lib-choice-preview), never on other surfaces: the ground sits in a choice item whose border and states are the choice list's.
Adapt
Light and dark values come from the theme (the colours are light-dark pairs; the shade switches with the theme). Forced colours drop the matrix.
Driven by
The page's filter (installPreviewFilter()) reads them through a probe element and rebuilds its matrix when the theme changes.

What

Copy and wording

Rule
Before

Point strength blends pigment across the shape. More blend softens differences between nearby points; a zero point may retain some pigment. Edge softness controls the outline separately.

After
What
Plain, calm, second person ("your V", "your game files"): what happens and what to do, never how it is implemented. Use the exact names on the controls, one name per thing (3D view, UV map, version, Settings › Game), and no developer words (host, server, SQLite, budget, provisional, LUT, "a Studio choice"). Limits: titles 1–3 words; labels 1–4; buttons 1–3, verb first, "…" when a choice follows; a status line one line (about 70 characters); an inline note one sentence (about 100); a help tip at most two short paragraphs (300 characters); a reason one sentence (about 90); a toast one or two sentences with its recovery button. The full rules and the audit are in research/authoring/ui-copy-and-layout-review.md.
When
Where text goes: what something is or how it works → a help tip on its label or heading; what the person can do now → an inline note on a reserved line or the status line, with the button; a changing state → the status line or the control's own label; a set of facts → a structured display (property list, chips); why a control is unavailable → its reason tip; an outcome → a toast; a designed but unbuilt feature → a disabled control with "Coming soon: " (no empty sections).
Combine
Honesty stays, briefly: "not yet checked in game" is one clause, once per place. Say a state in one place only.
Avoid
Repeating a label in the note under it, explaining what a visible control obviously does, naming a control that doesn't exist, a paragraph under a control, and text that moves the layout when it appears.

Spacing, sizing and density

Implemented
246812162028

Controls 28 px (24 px small) · rows 32 px · tabs 32 px · header 44 px · status 26 px.

What
A 2-px based scale. Panels use 12 px padding and 16 px between sections; related controls sit 8 px apart.
When
Keep one scale step between unrelated groups. Do not invent new heights; lists and menus rely on the shared row height for scanning.
Combine
Sections stack with --sp-6; controls inside a section with --sp-4; a toolbar row keeps --sp-2 between related buttons.
Adapt
Compact workspaces keep control sizes; they change arrangement (tabs, icon-only header actions), not target size.
Driven by
Tokens --sp-*, --control-h, --row-h, --tab-h, --header-h, --status-h.

Bevel, borders and elevation

Implemented
ChipBadge
Card7 px bevel
What
Bevelled corners via CSS corner-shape (top-right and bottom-left on controls; top-right on cards, menus, windows). Borders are 1 px; elevation is reserved for things above the dock: floating windows, menus, toasts and dialogs.
When
Bevel is the only decorative shape. Never combine it with rounded corners or drop shadows on docked panels.
Combine
A bevelled surface never nests inside another bevelled surface of the same size; cards inside panels are bevelled, the panel group is not.
Adapt
Browsers without corner-shape show square 2 px radii — the design must read correctly without the bevel.
Driven by
corner-shape: bevel with --bevel / --bevel-sm radii; --shadow only for layers above the dock.

Original 16 px line icons, square caps and mitred joins, drawn for this project. Stroke uses currentColor; filled marks are used only for dots and grips.

Motion

Implemented
Updating 2K140 ms ease-out
What
140 ms state transitions, a sweeping bar for indeterminate work and a two-step blink for updating previews. Drop previews ease 80 ms so targets feel magnetic without lag.
When
Motion only communicates state change or work in progress. Nothing loops except genuine ongoing work.
Combine
Progress bars sit directly under the action that started the work; readiness badges repeat the state where the result is seen (stage and status bar).
Adapt
Motion is identical at every size; reduced-motion users get instant state changes.
Driven by
--dur, --ease and the sweep/pulse keyframes; readiness phase from previewReadiness.
Keyboard & access
prefers-reduced-motion collapses all transitions and animations to 1 ms.

Focus and keyboard

Implemented
What
A 2 px ring in --focus (signal yellow on dark, ink on light) with 2 px offset; inside tab bars and lists the ring sits inset so it is never clipped.
When
Every interactive element shows focus-visible. Pointer clicks do not leave rings on buttons.
Combine
Focus follows the action: after closing a menu or popover it returns to the invoker; after a reorder it stays on the moved row.
Adapt
Identical in both themes and all sizes; the ring colour switches from yellow (dark) to ink (light) for ≥3:1 against adjacent colours.
Driven by
--focus token; roving tabindex in tab strips, rows and menus.
Keyboard & access
F6 cycles header → each panel group → status bar. Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the same context menu a right-click would.

Stage surround

Rule
Stage · both themes
What
Viewports use the same neutral radial surround in light and dark themes. Overlays on the stage use their own fixed colours (stage chip, stage text).
When
Any panel that shows the head, a texture or a material comparison.
Avoid
Theme-coloured backgrounds behind colour-critical content.
02

Shell and navigation

The shell has three bands: a header that names where you are and holds the few global commitments, a dock workspace that owns everything else, and a status bar that tells the truth about saving, work in progress and preview readiness.

Application header

Implemented
XFStudio
Eye makeup
Night market setChrome duskSaved
Verification workspace
What
Brand, the authoring category (a plain label while there is only one; the switcher later), a breadcrumb of collection › preset with the library state chip, the verification flag when isolated, and global actions: Undo, Redo and History (grouped; their tooltips name the step each would change, such as “Redo: Move point (Ctrl+Shift+Z)”, and keep the shortcut visible while unavailable), Save to library, Package, command palette, panels/layout and theme.
When
Always visible. Only commands that act on the whole document or workspace belong here; anything about a layer or panel stays in that panel.
Combine
The library chip repeats the Presets panel chip so saved state is visible when that panel is closed.
Adapt
Below 1100 px the brand word, collection crumb and action labels collapse to icons with names; below 720 px the chip and verification flag hide (the status bar still reports them).
Driven by
library.summary(), authoring.capability({kind:'history.undo'|'history.redo'}), authoring.history(), authoring.requestCapability({kind:'save'}), status.snapshot().verification, preferences.

Category label and growth

Implemented
Eye makeup
What
The header names the authoring category. It is the one place new categories will join. With only Eye makeup there is nothing to choose, so it is a plain label, not a menu: menus list only what can be done.
When
It becomes a switcher (a menu with one item per category) only when a second category has its own approved data model, actions and panels.
Combine
Selecting a category will swap the panel registry and default layouts (see the future-category composition); shared panels such as Library and Package stay.
Adapt
Compact headers show only the icon and chevron; the menu content is the same.
Driven by
Static today; a future category registry would supply entries with their own panel registries and actions.
Avoid
A menu with nothing to choose, sections that only inform, listing unbuilt categories, or turning preview-context toggles (brows, hair) into authoring entries.

Status bar

Implemented
Gesture in progress · Esc cancelsPreview 2K · updating
What
Draft autosave state, the latest activity or in-flight library message (click opens Activity), gesture/transaction hints and preview readiness.
When
Always visible. It reports; it never hosts commands other than opening the activity log.
Combine
The message slot mirrors the newest Activity entry; readiness mirrors the 3D view badge; errors also toast so they are not missed.
Adapt
Messages truncate with an ellipsis; the Activity panel keeps the full text.
Driven by
status.snapshot().workspace, library.summary().progress, previewState().gesture/control, previewReadiness.snapshot().
Keyboard & access
Toasts and the activity log carry the same messages to assistive technology through live regions; the status bar itself is not a live region to avoid double announcements.

03

Panel system

Fixed sidebars are gone. Every functional area is a panel that can be docked, floated, grouped as tabs or magnetically joined with other floating panels. Snapping is decided by where the cursor is — never by the dragged panel's size or position — so a large panel passing over others never snaps by accident. The live sandbox and live dock at the end of this section run the production engine.

Docked tab group

Implemented

Presets

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

Colour & finish

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

What
A group shows one panel at a time behind a tab strip. The active tab carries the ink/yellow indicator and a close control; the empty strip to the right is the group's drag handle; ⋯ opens layout options.
When
Put panels in one group when they are used alternately (Presets / Library / Package) and side by side when they are used together (Head and UV map).
Combine
Groups sit in splits. When a strip runs short its tabs condense in stages (the tab strip component, lib-tab-strip): inactive labels cut short, then inactive tabs icon-only (right) while the active label stays readable, then the active one too, then an overflow menu. Every tab keeps its name as its tooltip and accessible name, and the header's collapse and layout buttons never shrink.
Adapt
Wide and compact workspaces keep separate arrangements. In compact layouts, most panels share two groups.
Driven by
Pure layout state (DockTree) saved through the workspace preference action layout.set; no application data.
Keyboard & access
role=tablist/tab/tabpanel; ←/→/Home/End switch tabs, Alt+Shift+←/→ reorders, Delete closes, Enter or ↓ moves into the panel, Shift+F10 opens layout options. Focus inside a group outlines it in cyan.

Summoning a panel

Implemented

UV map

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

Help

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

What
Every way of asking for a panel (the command palette, the Panels menu, the Help button, a tour step, a link from another panel) summons it the same way, so it is always shown and focused. Already in an expanded group: its tab becomes active. In a collapsed group: the group expands with its tab active. Not in the layout: it goes back to an obvious home, which is where it was when it was closed (its group at its tab position, beside its old neighbour, or its floating window) or the group it belongs to in the factory layout; with no obvious home it opens in a floating window over the middle of the workspace. It is never dropped into an arbitrary group, least of all a collapsed one (left: Help summoned while the right column's lower group is folded opens floating, right).
When
Always; features never place panels themselves. A panel closed by default (Help, Activity) has no home, so it floats until the person docks it; after that, closing and summoning it again returns it to where they put it.
Combine
Focus moves to the panel's tab, or into the panel when its opener focuses something there (Help focuses its search). The result is announced: “Help opened in a floating window”, “Colour & finish expanded, showing Shape”.
Adapt
Where it was closed from is remembered per size class with the layout (lastPlace); a panel opened by any other route forgets it. A floating panel is clamped on screen like any window.
Driven by
summonPanel(tree, panel, factory, floatRect) in studio-ui/dock/layout.ts, through DockView.reveal. Tests: tests/dock-summon.test.ts.
Keyboard & access
The summoned tab (or the control its opener chose) receives focus; the announcement says where the panel went.

Splits and splitters

Implemented
What
Rows and columns of groups with 4 px splitters. Hover or focus shows the cyan track; dragging resizes the two neighbours only.
When
Any docked arrangement. Minimum group size is 150 × 96 px.
Combine
Splits hold groups or further splits; a group's minimum size stops a splitter before content collapses.
Adapt
Sizes are fractions, so resizing the window scales every column and row proportionally.
Driven by
DockTree split nodes (axis, sizes) via setSizes().
Keyboard & access
Splitters are focusable separators: arrow keys move 4 %, Enter or double-click equalises the pair.

Collapsed group: header row or vertical strip

Implemented
What
A collapsed group keeps only its tab bar. Folded along a column it is a header row spanning the column (right). Folded along a row (a group alone in its row, or a column whose groups all collapsed) it is a full-height vertical strip: the same tab bar turned on its side (left to right: the first tab active, a middle tab active, a shorter strip with the inactive tabs icon-only, and the shortest with every tab icon-only). Each tab has padding at both ends, an upright icon centred across the strip, a gap between icon, label and close mark, and a hairline between tabs; the active tab is raised to the panel surface with the yellow indicator down the strip's outer edge and its close mark as its own 18 px target at its end.
When
Collapse a group to keep its panels one click away while giving its space to the rest of the workspace. Choosing any tab expands the group showing that tab.
Combine
The strip condenses in the same stages as a crowded bar (the tab strip component, lib-tab-strip): full labels, inactive labels cut short, inactive tabs icon-only, the active tab icon-only, then an overflow menu at the strip's end. An icon-only tab keeps its name as its tooltip and accessible name, and a label is never cut mid-glyph. The expand and layout buttons sit at the strip's foot and never shrink.
Adapt
The strip is 36 px wide (the 32 px bar height plus 4 px), whichever tab is active or hovered, so nothing shifts. Its tabs refit whenever its height changes.
Driven by
foldAxes in studio-ui/dock/layout.ts picks the axis; the dock marks the group data-fold and builds its header with orientation: "vertical". The tab CSS is written in logical properties, so writing-mode: vertical-rl on the strip turns padding, separators and the indicator with it. Tests: tests/dock-collapse-dom.test.ts (folding), tests/dock-strip-geometry.test.ts (laid-out geometry in Chrome: no overlaps, padding, centred icons, one width, icon-only fallback).
Keyboard & access
The tablist is marked aria-orientation=vertical and keeps the bar's keys (←/→/Home/End switch tabs). The focus ring is drawn inside each tab (outline offset −2 px), so the strip's clipping never cuts it.

Floating panel

Implemented

Camera

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

What
A panel in its own window above the dock, with resize handles on every edge and corner. Its tab strip is the window's title bar.
When
Temporary tools you want next to the stage without reflowing the docked layout (lighting while judging a finish, Motion while checking closed lids).
Combine
Floating windows can attach to each other (composites) or return to any group. They stay above a maximized group.
Adapt
Windows are clamped so at least their title bar remains reachable after window resize or restore.
Driven by
DockTree.floating windows (x, y, w, h, node) via applyDrop({kind:'float'}), setWindowRect(), raiseWindow() and recoverWindows().
Keyboard & access
Panel menu › Move or resize window… enters a keyboard mode: arrows move (Ctrl for fine steps), Shift+arrows resize, Enter or Escape ends and saves.

Magnetic composite

Implemented
2 panels · magnetic composite
What
Two or more floating groups joined edge to edge into one window. A thin bar moves the whole composite; each member keeps its own tabs and can be dragged out again.
When
When a set of floating tools belongs together (motion + lighting while reviewing on a moving face).
Combine
Join by dragging a panel until the cursor enters the magnetic band along a floating window's edge (18 px either side of the edge) or onto its compass arrows. The composite grows to make room instead of squeezing its content.
Adapt
A composite keeps its members' proportions when resized; if a member leaves, the window returns that member's share.
Driven by
A floating window whose node is a split; created by applyDrop with a split target on a floating group.
Keyboard & access
Panel menu › Place beside › (floating group) › Attach left/right/above/below. Composite menu › Dock composite to edge or Merge into group as tabs.

Drag feedback: cursor targets

Implemented
Motion

The cursor (yellow square) is on the compass's left arrow, so the preview fills the left half: “Split left”. The ghost only labels what is moving; its size is irrelevant.

What
While dragging, the group under the cursor shows a five-way compass (centre = add as tab; arrows = split beside). Edge guides at the middle of each workspace edge dock to the full edge. Tab strips accept tabs at the cursor's insertion point. Floating windows add a magnetic edge band. The cyan preview shows exactly where the panel will land and names the result.
When
Drop outside every guide to float the panel where you release it. Hold Ctrl to float freely even over a guide. Escape cancels the drag and restores a moved window.
Combine
The preview is the contract: whatever it names is what happens on release, and the result is announced to screen readers.
Adapt
Guides are fixed-size (34 px) at any workspace size; edge guides stay reachable in compact layouts; previews are computed from the actual target rectangle.
Driven by
resolveDrop(cursor, geometry) in studio-ui/dock/snap.ts — inputs are the cursor point and the rectangles of target groups/guides; the dragged panel's rectangle is not a parameter. Unit tests assert that a large overlapping panel does not snap until the cursor reaches a target.

Live snapping sandbox

Implemented

Load this guide in a browser with scripts enabled to try the production snap resolver.

Drag the large “Lighting” panel. It only snaps when the cursor — not the panel — reaches a guide.

What
The production resolver running on three sample groups. The dragged panel is deliberately large so it overlaps targets while the cursor stays outside them.
When
Use it to reason about new guide placements before changing snap.ts; keep the unit tests in tests/dock-layout.test.ts in step.
Combine
Pairs with d-feedback: the static specimen explains the vocabulary, the sandbox lets you test it.
Adapt
Fixed 360 px area; resolution uses real measured rectangles.
Driven by
resolveDrop() and previewRect() from src/studio-ui/dock/snap.ts.

Implemented

Maximized · Restore button in the tab bar

Every panel is floating or closed.

Double-click a tab bar (or use its menu) to maximize a group over the dock; floating windows stay available. If every panel is floating or closed, the dock shows an explanation and Reset.
When
Maximize for close inspection of the head or UV map; restore the same way.
Combine
The maximized group keeps its tab strip and a Restore button; floating windows stay above it.
Adapt
Most useful in compact windows for the 3D view or UV map.

DockTree.maximized via setMaximized().

Always available; the command palette also offers Go to/Open and Float for every panel, and the Panels menu toggles each panel.

Size classes and default layouts

Implemented
What
Two independently remembered arrangements. Crossing 1100 px switches between them without losing either; Reset restores the current size class only. Activity is closed by default and opens from the status bar.
When
Design new panels for both: say which default group they join in each size class. Keep the head's default cell portrait (it is a portrait subject and front framing fits its width) and the UV map's cell wide enough for the 720:310 both-eyes view, with both visible at once.
Combine
A new panel names its shell slot in its view contribution, which places it in both size classes; missing panels rejoin their default siblings on restore.
Adapt
The header condenses labels; the dock does not reflow panels automatically within a size class — users own their arrangement.
Driven by
defaultWide(), defaultCompact(), COMPACT_BREAKPOINT and DockState {wide, compact}.

Saved layouts

Implemented
Layouts
MaximisedChanged · In wide windows
LaptopIn compact windows
PosingChanged
Eye makeup
Save changes
Revert to saved
Save as new layout…
Rename…
Delete

What
Named panel arrangements (view-graph-design.md §4.5), from the header's Layouts button (its stacked-windows icon and the current layout's name, the icon alone in narrow windows; tooltip Layout: name) and the palette (Layout: name, Save layout…, Save changes, Revert, Rename, Delete, Reset to factory layout). A layout holds both size classes' arrangements, floating windows, collapsed groups, active tabs and parked places, and by default which modules show. Switching is instant and asks nothing: a changed layout keeps its changes when you switch away and shows them again when you come back; Revert to saved brings the saved arrangement back, Save changes keeps the new one. Rows say only what is different (Changed, In compact windows); the check marks the current layout. Commands are grouped: saving, the library, the layout's options, the factory reset. While nothing changed, Save changes and Revert say so in the muted tone (quietReason).
When
One layout per way of working (maximised and laptop windows, eye makeup and posing). A layout can be chosen for wide or compact windows and is switched to when the window crosses into that size; a layout picked by hand stays until the window changes size class again. Delete offers Undo in its notice instead of asking first.
Combine
Names are entered in the value popover with its options (c-popover): the name has a default, Remember shown modules is on, Switch to it automatically is off. Module switches only park and unpark panels; work is never affected.
Adapt
The header button shows the layout name (cut short when it is long) and only its icon below 1100 px; the menu is the same in every window.
Driven by
layouts.saveAs | update | revert | switch | rename | duplicate | delete | insert | setModules | setAutoSize | seen through preferences.dispatch; DockView.load; sameDockState decides what counts as changed.
Keyboard & access
A menu button named with the layout and its state; the layouts are checkable entries; unavailable commands say why, muted where it is information rather than a problem (No changes since it was saved; This is your only layout).

Persistence and recovery

Implemented
What
Layouts persist as a versioned, bounded workspace preference (format xfs/dock, version 1) beside theme choice — never in recipes, collections, SQLite or exports. Saved layouts (xfs/layout-library-1) are kept in the same preferences.
When
Restored at start through the ui-preferences recovery gate: malformed trees are rejected, unknown panels (a newer build's) kept parked with their places, duplicates removed, missing (new) panels re-added beside their default siblings, and floating windows pulled back on screen. Invalid saved layouts fall back to defaults with a visible notice.
Combine
Theme preference is stored beside the layout; both change without touching recipes, Undo or the library.
Adapt
Each size class is recovered against the current window, so a layout saved on a large monitor opens safely on a laptop.
Driven by
preferences.dispatch({kind:'layout.set', layout}), recoverDockLayout, parseTree, recoverWindows.

The production DockView with sample panels: drag tabs and tab bars, float, attach, split, resize, close and reopen from the ⋯ menus. Its layout is not saved.

Try interactions here before changing dock-view.ts; the Studio uses the same class with real panels.

Menus, drags and splitters behave exactly as in the Studio.

04

Components

Components are presentation only. Each one names the application action or read-only state behind it, and shows the application's reason when it is unavailable. Nothing here owns validation, Undo, persistence or export decisions.

Buttons

Implemented
Choose your Cyberpunk 2077 folder in Game & tools first.
What
Primary (yellow, one per region: the commitment), default, quiet (secondary in a region), ghost (tool clusters), danger (destructive where Undo is not enough) and small/icon-only variants. Toggle tools use aria-pressed; a quiet button that holds a state (Poses: Stand still, Idle) shows it pressed in cyan (text, fill and edge), so no status line need repeat it.
When
Primary marks the action that records or produces something (Save to library, Build). Never two primaries side by side.
Combine
Icon + verb label. Icon-only buttons are allowed in tool clusters and row trailing actions, always with an accessible name and tooltip.
Adapt
Header actions collapse to icon-only buttons below 1100 px; panel buttons wrap onto new rows rather than shrinking.
Driven by
Availability = the action's capability. An unavailable main action keeps its place and its focus, and states the application's reason (the command palette and menus show the same text).
Keyboard & access
The menu pattern (UI-84): an unavailable button is aria-disabled, not disabled, so keyboard, touch and screen-reader users reach it. Its reason is its accessible description and appears as a tip on focus, hover or tap; a click runs nothing. Native disabled stays for form fields.

Chips, badges and status vocabulary

Implemented
SavedNot saved yetNewer version savedWorking…
Can be builtPreview onlyCurrentStale — draft changed sinceBlocked
What
Chips describe document/library state; badges qualify a result or capability. The words are fixed vocabulary: Working, Preview only, Can be built, Current, Stale, Blocked. A finished Build states its limits in one plain sentence (built and checked, not tested in game, nothing installed) rather than in badges.
When
Whenever a result could be mistaken for more than it is. A green badge never implies game rendering.
Combine
The library chip sits beside the preset name in the header and under the collection name in Presets; result badges sit in the result card's head.
Adapt
Chips hide below 720 px in the header only; the Presets panel keeps them.
Driven by
libraryState() from library.summary(); result badges from files.snapshot().package.
Avoid
Colour-only status dots without words; vague labels like “OK” or “Done”.

Text, title and select fields

Implemented
What
Sunken inputs with a strong boundary. Names commit on Enter or blur and revert on Escape; the application validates (e.g. 1–120 characters) and a refused rename restores the previous name with a toast.
When
Inline rename in rows (F2 / double-click), the collection title in Presets, value popovers and selects for enumerations with few choices.
Combine
A field is always paired with a visible label or an accessible name; inline rename replaces the row's button in place.
Adapt
Fields fill their column; titles truncate with an ellipsis rather than wrapping.
Driven by
collection.rename, preset.edit rename, layer.edit rename; application validation decides.
Keyboard & access
Native text inputs keep the browser's text context menu; Studio suppresses native menus only on non-text surfaces.

Slider with readout (one Undo per drag)

Implemented
Enable smooth point gradients to adjust blending.
What
Range input with a monospaced readout. Pointer down or arrow keys begin a control transaction, every value is an edit, release/blur commits one Undo step, and Escape restores the starting value.
When
Continuous recipe values (opacity, pigment, softness, reach, flake settings) and view preferences (FOV, exposure).
Combine
Pair related sliders in one row only when both fit (Colour + Opacity); disabled sliders keep their reason directly beneath.
Adapt
Sliders fill their column; readouts never wrap.
Driven by
authoring.controlBegin(id, layerId) → controlEdit(id, action) → controlCommit(id) / controlCancel(id). Ranges come from actionDescriptors() limits, not UI constants.
Keyboard & access
The label is the input's label. A control's note line never moves the layout (UI-90): once a control has a note it keeps the line (an empty note keeps its height, a disabled reason takes its place); a control without one says why it is disabled in its tooltip and description, and its panel says it once.

Expanders (one disclosure for every level)

Implemented

What
One expander folds everything that folds: the parts of V (group), their sections, a section's subsections, rows and the author groups inside a row. Every level has the same chevron (10 px, pointing right when folded and down when open, turning without moving anything), the same gap between chevron and text, and the same hover and focus. Only the type steps down, in one hierarchy: group (display face, uppercase, the largest) › section (display, uppercase) › subsection (display, uppercase, muted, one step in) › row (UI face, sentence case: content, not a heading) › author group (UI face, sentence case, the smallest, with its count). A section with rows has Expand all / Collapse all at the far right of its heading, after its show/hide switch; its icon and name say what a press does now. A folded heading holding search matches shows how many.
When
Any foldable hierarchy: the Character panel now; later feature panels with grouped rows. Never build a second chevron style.
Combine
A heading row is: expander, help tip (when it has one), then at the far right its switch and Expand all. Author groups with a single choice in the row share one Other mods group, last, sorted by label; each choice's mod is in its tooltip.
Adapt
Labels truncate to one line; the switch and Expand all never wrap below the heading.
Driven by
Presentation state: every fold (a group's, a section's, a row's and an author group's) is remembered across reloads in the workspace's view state (lib-view-state: the expanded.set {keys, expanded} UI preference, never Undo, not part of a layout); a row whose mod isn't loaded keeps its state until it shows. Expand all opens the section's rows and unfolds their author groups; the palette offers it per section and folds or opens every section.
Keyboard & access
The WAI disclosure pattern: a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, inside the heading element of its level (h3–h5), so headings keep their outline. Enter or Space folds; an author-group heading also folds with Left and unfolds with Right from inside its listbox. Expand all is an icon button named for what it will do.

Help tips (what something is)

Implemented

Files

A save is read on this computer and never changed or uploaded.

What
A small help icon beside a heading, row or control holds what it is or does (hair physics is not simulated; a row follows a switcher; what a save import touches) in a rich tooltip: an optional bold title and short paragraphs. Inline text is kept for what the person can act on: a status with Try again, a choice to make, why something failed. One tip for the page floats above everything, so showing it never moves the layout.
When
Every panel, instead of an informational note under a heading or control. A control's help and a section's { title, help } produce it.
Combine
Beside the label, outside it (pressing the icon never works the control). An empty help keeps the icon's place hidden, so a row's layout doesn't jump when its shown option has nothing to say.
Adapt
The tip is at most 300 px wide and stays inside the window, below the icon or above it near the bottom.
Driven by
Static or read-only text only; setHelp(icon, text) changes it in place (the Body switch's help follows the uncensored setting).
Keyboard & access
The icon is a button in the tab order named “About ”; its text is the button's accessible description, read on focus without opening anything. The tip shows on focus or hover and pins open on a click or tap; Escape, a second click or leaving closes it. It never takes focus and holds no controls.

Creator options (generated rows)

Implemented
Updating…

Not prepared yet · Preparing

What
Every creator option of the shown V, generated from the installed game and mods, in one hierarchy: the parts of V (Head, Body, Clothing), then the panel's own sections (Head: Skin; Face with Eyes, Eyebrows, Eyelashes, Nose, Mouth & lips, Ears, Jaw & shape, Makeup, Piercings and Face details inside; Hair; Teeth; Other), where each row lands by what it controls (the preview detail its slot feeds, then the words of its slot, option names and link keys, then the category the game or mod declared), never by display name or a per-mod table, then rows of options sharing a creator slot (the active one shows), and the active option's choices opened in place, as a swatch grid for colours and chips otherwise, Off first. Every colour choice, the game's or a mod's, is a narrow swatch: the game's icon (unless a mod replaced that colour's resource), else the colour derived from the resource that wins for it (a hair, brow or lash profile as a small root-to-tip gradient), else the definition's colour. A tightly clustered set of derived colours (one maker's group, or the row) is shown spread apart in lightness and hue, in order; the row's own chip keeps the true colour, and a contrast help tip (a half-filled circle) beside the row's help tip says the list shows more contrast. Resting on a swatch, or focusing it, shows the swatch card (lib-swatch-card): its true colour, name and maker. What the 3D view shows is part of the same hierarchy: each section has at most one show/hide switch, on its heading, for what it draws; why it can't change is the reason tip, and what it shows is the heading's help tip. Everything folds with the shared expander (c-expanders); what a row or heading is lives in help tips (c-help-tips), never an inline line. A changed row is marked and offers Reset to the V's own; an option with an Off choice offers Off; a row whose choice the 3D view doesn't draw shows a fixed-size marker. The search finds options and choices on the host, over every choice. An open row's choices are prepared ahead in the background, the ones in view first: a choice not prepared yet carries a small hollow corner mark, the one being prepared a turning cyan mark, one that couldn't be prepared ahead a filled warning mark, and a ready one none. One short line under the search names the marks; what they mean is its help tip.
When
The Character panel. The prominent action, Hide my V's own makeup, and Reset all sit above the rows; everything else is per row.
Combine
One status line of fixed height above (never moves the layout): Updating… (for a choice that wasn't prepared ahead, why it takes a few seconds the first time), what failed, or the first of the plain lines about what couldn't be used, clamped to one line; Try again, Keep my changes and Details keep their place when not offered. Undo and Redo for creator changes sit beside the V's source; they are separate from the makeup's history.
Adapt
Single column at every width; row values and the status line truncate, never wrap; the swatch grid fills the row with as many columns as fit.
Driven by
character.setOption (with a switcher choice's activated options), character.setOwnMakeup (the V's own makeup, a switch), character.reset, character.resetAll, character.keepChanges, character.retry, character.undo/redo; authoring.characterPanel(), characterView(), characterChoices(option, want, query) and characterSearch(query) (frozen, paged), characterPrefetch(option, positions, focus) and characterStopPrefetch(option) (each choice's prepared-ahead state, polled per row), characterSwatches(option) (a colour row's derived swatches and icons), a row's choices grouped by maker under folding headings when they come from more than one (the projection's groups and modGroups), heading switches from characterPanelTree contributions (preview.setDetail/setHair/setPiercings/setBody, character.setClothing), preview.setUncensored in Body, character.clearPreparedFiles under Files, coverage notes from the preview's projection.
Keyboard & access
Rows are buttons with aria-expanded and an accessible description (where the option comes from, the V's own choice, whether the 3D view draws it). Choices are a listbox: arrow keys, Home and End move focus without choosing (each choice prepares the V anew), Enter or Space chooses; the chosen one is aria-selected by identity, and each choice's origin is its accessible description. Choosing keeps focus on the same item. A choice's prepared-ahead state joins its accessible description and tooltip ("not prepared yet", "being prepared"); the marks are decoration (aria-hidden in the legend), sit in the item's corner so they never move the layout, keep their own fill to stay legible over any swatch in both themes, and stop turning under reduced motion. Hovering or focusing a choice prepares it next. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y inside the panel step the character's own history. A heading switch is named for what it shows ("Show hair in the 3D view"); when it can't change it stays focusable with aria-disabled, and its reason is its description and the page's reason tip.

Add to my mod manager (review, then consent)

Implemented

Add “XF Eye Artistry” to Mod Organizer 2?

Adds XF Eye Artistry in Mod Organizer 2 (profile “Main”). Nothing is added until you choose Add to Mod Organizer 2.

  • Add the mod “XF Eye Artistry” to Mod Organizer 2, with its 2 files in …\MO2\mods\XF Eye Artistry\archive\pc\mod.
  • Add “XF Eye Artistry” to the profile “Main”, switched on. At the bottom of the "Looks" section, where Mod Organizer puts newly installed mods.
  • Nothing else in your mod list changes.

Mod Organizer 2 is open. Close it first, then try again: it rewrites its mod list when it closes, and would undo this.

What
The review before an install: exactly what would be added and where (the mod's own folder and the one mod-list row with its section, or the game's archive\pc\mod folder), what to know first, and why it can't be done now with the one next step. The host refuses folders XF Studio didn't create and files it didn't put there, never touches frameworks or other mods, and refuses a plan that no longer matches (then the sheet reviews again).

The sheet is at most 640 px wide with a 16 px gutter; long folder paths wrap anywhere rather than widening it.

What
Blender-style help that follows the pointer and the held keys. Each viewport has a fixed corner strip: what drag, wheel, double-click and right-drag do on the target under the pointer, the viewport keys, and "Hold Shift / Ctrl / Alt" discovery. Holding a modifier switches the strip at once (the held key leads, accent-edged); an active drag or wheel burst shows its gesture with Release/Pause and Esc. Resting on makeup shows a tooltip naming the target and its bindings for the held keys. The cursor comes from the same binding: grab on handles, move on a shape, a rotate glyph with Shift over makeup, a scale glyph during a Shift-wheel burst, all-scroll while Ctrl pans, and the plain cursor where Shift does nothing. Hover a swatch to try each cursor on the stage and a light surface.
When
3D view and UV map panels, on by default. View preferences › Show input hints (also in the Keyboard & mouse dialog and the palette) hides the strip and tooltips; cursors stay because they describe the gesture itself.
Combine
Never interactive (pointer-events: none) and never covering the stage centre: the strip overlays the bottom-left corner of both stages, beside the readiness badge on the head. The UV map's Fit keeps a band clear for it. Its last item points to the ? Keyboard & mouse dialog.
Adapt
The strip wraps within 72% of the head stage (the full width of the UV stage) and is clamped to two rows; items that do not fit are clipped, never pushing the canvas; below 720 px the Hold/? discovery group hides and only what the pointer does now remains. The tooltip flips to stay inside the panel.
Driven by
Derived only from src/input-bindings.ts: viewportHints(), targetTip() and cursorFor() over the read-only viewport.input() snapshot (held modifiers plus each adapter's hover target and gesture), on its own viewport.subscribeInput channel; preferences.inputHints. The gesture adapters resolve the same bindings, so hint, cursor and behaviour cannot disagree.
Keyboard & access
Not a live region (it changes with every hover); the same bindings are in each viewport's accessible name and the Keyboard & mouse dialog. Both strips use the theme-aware --stage-* tokens. Custom cursors are white glyphs with a dark halo and fall back to grab / nwse-resize keywords; blur or a hidden page clears held modifiers. Reduced motion removes the tooltip fade.

05

Component library

Every component panels and features compose, with its full contract: purpose, anatomy, variants, states, sizes, how it adapts, keyboard and access, do and avoid, and a composition example. Import from src/studio-ui/components. Each specimen is built live by the production component.

Component-first UI

Rule
What
All UI is composed from this library. Panels and feature views compose components and wire them to actions and snapshots; they do not build controls (buttons, fields, lists, tabs, dialogs, progress) from raw elements. Components that only one feature needs still live in the library, in the Feature-specific category.
When
A feature that needs a control the library lacks specifies it (behaviour, states, accessibility) and the UI component track builds or extends it here, with its entry on this page. tests/ui-component-ratchet.test.ts counts the ad hoc controls left outside the library per file: no file may gain one, and each count only goes down.
Categories
General: Button, Icon button, Switch, Slider, Slider with value, Pair control, Bipolar slider, Scrub slider, Segmented control, Choice list, Choice preview, Choice layouts, Colour field, Select field, Combobox, Search field, Expander, Group section, Help tip, Reason tip, Menu, value and confirm popovers, Ordered list, Tab strip, Panel header, Badge, note, empty state and progress, Tree view, Remembered view state, Folder setting
Layout: Layout primitives, Split view, Splitter
Feature-specific: Light list, Direction dial, Swatch card

Button

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A command with a verb label and an optional icon: the default control for doing something.
Module
studio-ui/controls.ts · button, applyCapability · General
Anatomy
Bevelled box · optional leading icon · label (a span) · nothing else. Icon-only drops the label and keeps it as the accessible name and tooltip.
Variants
default, primary (one per region), quiet, ghost (tool clusters), danger; small; iconOnly; menu (opens a menu: aria-haspopup).
States
rest, hover, active, focus-visible, pressed (aria-pressed for a tool toggle), unavailable (the main-action pattern: aria-disabled with its reason).
Sizes
28 px (--control-h), small 24 px (--control-h-sm); icon-only is square.
When
Any action in panel content, headers, sheets and toasts.
Combine
A row of actions: h("div", { class: "row wrap gap-s" }, button({ label: "Check", icon: "check", onClick }), button({ label: "Build", variant: "primary", onClick })). A toast's actions and a sheet's footer are buttons too.
Adapt
Labels never wrap; a crowded header shows icon-only buttons with the label as tooltip and name.
Driven by
Availability is the action's capability: applyCapability(control, capability).
Keyboard & access
Native button; Enter and Space. An unavailable one stays focusable, says why (its description and the page's reason tip) and runs nothing when pressed.
Do
Start the label with a verb; use one primary per region; mark menu triggers with menu.
Avoid
Building h("button", { class: "btn" }) by hand (it skips the unavailable guard); native disabled on a main action; two primaries side by side.
See also
c-buttons

Anatomy
24 px square (22 px small) · one 16 px icon · no border until hover.
Variants
small; menu (aria-haspopup); pressed (a toggle, coloured signal when on); mode (with pressed: a mode such as mirrored sides, tinted as well when on, so it reads at a glance); expanded (a disclosure); className for placement hooks.
States

Adapt
Fixed size at every width.
Driven by
The owner's intent (close, open a menu, toggle); availability via applyCapability.
Keyboard & access
Named by label, titled by it too unless title says more; menu triggers announce their popup; toggles announce their state.

Give every icon button a label that names the action and its object ("Hide Petal wash"). Use mode for a mode the person turns on for a region, not for per-row marks that are on by default.

Hand-built .icon-btn elements; an icon button without a tooltip.

Anatomy

default; set (away from its default: the label emphasised with a signal mark, the reset shown); dragging; typing an exact value; the owner's readout; disabled (its reason on the note line when reserved, else in the tooltip and description).

Label line 22 px; track as Slider; about 44 px a control stacked, 22 px inline, so a list of them stays dense at 300 px.

Values people also type, with a meaningful default (expression and shape values).

Rows of them inside a Group section; two inline ones make a Pair control's separate state. A list of them shares one disabled reason, said once by the panel.

Full width; the label truncates with an ellipsis before the readout or reset would move.
Driven by
The Slider's transaction for drags; a typed value, Delete or the reset is one begin/edit/commit step, clamped and snapped to the step.

Give it the default so people can see what they changed.
Avoid
A number box beside the slider; a reserved note line under every row of a list; a faded reset on every row.

Direction dial

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
Where a light sits around V, seen from above: one handle whose angle round the dial is the light's direction and whose distance from the centre is its height, with a height scale beside it that says the height as a number.
Module
studio-ui/components/direction-dial.ts · DirectionDial, dialPoint, dialDirection, dragDirection, snapStep, heightTicks, heightY, fitDialSize, azimuthWords, DIAL_MIN_SIZE, DIAL_DEFAULT_SIZE, HEIGHT_SNAP · Feature-specific
Anatomy
Label line with two readouts (the angle, the height), each typed into in place · a round dial: V's head at the centre with her nose toward the bottom edge ("Front"), "Behind" at the top, "V's right" upright on the left and "V's left" on the right as when you face her, a dashed ring for level with the head, the edge for straight below · the handle in the light's colour · the setup's other lights as small dots · a vertical height scale on the right (+89° to −89°, labelled ticks at the ends, the quarters and level; the current height marked with a pointer and its value in the light's colour) · while dragging, a dashed radius from the centre to the edge through the handle, the other dots dimmed · a resize bar under the dial · note line only on request.
Variants
elevation range (default −89° to 89°); reserveNote; others dots on or off; onResize to keep the chosen size.
States
rest; dragging (the radius line shows, the other dots dim; Shift keeps the angle, Alt snaps the height to 15°; Escape restores the start); keyboard burst (the same radius and dimming); typing an exact angle or height; resizing (the bar's grip lit); focus-visible (the dial's ring, the bar's ring); unavailable with its reason on the note line.
Sizes
The drawing is 180 px wide at least and 280 px by default; the resize bar sets it (kept as the controlSize.set UI preference under lighting-direction), clamped to the control's width, and drawn smaller while the panel is narrower (fitDialSize). Resize bar 12 px tall. Only the drawing scales: its words and ticks stay --fs-2xs and the current height --fs-xs mono at every size (counter-scaled by --dial-unit).
When
A light's direction in the lighting setup editor. A single angle alone is a Slider with value.
Combine
Under the Light list's selected light, above its distance and strength: new DirectionDial({ label: "Direction", transaction, onResize: (size, final) => final && keep(size) }), then update({ azimuth, elevation }, { colour, others, size }).
Adapt
Keeps its aspect; the chosen size shrinks to the control's width when the panel narrows and returns when it widens; centred; the readouts stay on the label line; the layout below moves only by the dial's own size.
Driven by
A begin/edit/commit/cancel transaction of { azimuth, elevation } in degrees: a drag or a keyboard burst is one transaction, a typed value one step. onResize(size, final) reports the chosen width; the owner keeps it on release. The owner turns the direction into the light's placement about the head.
Keyboard & access
The dial is one tab stop, role=slider with the angle as its value and "330°, from the front, V's left, 20° up" as its value text. Left and Right turn by 5°, Page Up and Page Down by 15°, Up and Down raise and lower by 5° (Alt: to the next 15° step), Home brings it to the front, Enter types the angle. The readouts are named "<label> angle, exact value" and "<label> height, exact value". The resize bar is its own tab stop, role=separator named "Resize <label>" with the width as its value: Up and Down shrink and enlarge by 16 px, Home and End go to the smallest and largest.
Do
Show the light's own colour on the handle and the height marker and its neighbours as dots, so the rig reads at a glance.
Avoid
Raw x, y, z fields for a light's position; two unrelated sliders for angle and height; a height scale without the current value marked.
See also
lib-light-list, lib-slider-value

Choice preview

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A picture of a choice drawn in the UI's own palette, for rows whose choices differ in shape or pattern (hairstyles first; brows, makeup, piercings, body kinds and poses later, research/character-customization/choice-previews-design.md). Pictures are diagrams, not photographs: a neutral subject, the choice in one ink, one soft light and one frame per row, so a long cut runs out of the frame and a pixie cut doesn't.
Module
studio-ui/components/choice-preview.ts · previewTile, PreviewSpin, SPIN, installPreviewFilter, previewTokens, PREVIEW_FILTER_IDS · General
Anatomy
Inside a choiceItem (which draws the border and the chosen, hover and focus states): a frame of the flat --pv-ground, bevelled top-right and bottom-left · the picture (a theme-free channel image coloured by an SVG colour matrix per theme from --pv-subject, --pv-ink and --pv-shade) · the label (--fs-2xs, muted, one line) · the prepared-ahead corner mark of the creator's choices.
Variants
Grid sizes S (56 px, label visually hidden: accessible name and tooltip only), M (88 px, the hairstyle default), L (132 px); list (28 px beside the label and source) and details (64 px with the prepared state) rows, see Choice layouts (lib-choice-layouts). Square aspect for hair; 2:1 and 1:2 for later kinds.
States
waiting (the frame and a faint glyph for the kind, never a spinner: the corner mark says the choice is being prepared) · ready (the picture fades in over --dur, at once under reduced motion) · none (no picture possible: the glyph stays, no error in the tile) · turning (grid L and details only: the pointer resting on the picture turns it slowly after 400 ms, one turn in 8 s, never under reduced motion; pressing and dragging turns it by hand at once, with the grab cursor; a drag never chooses, a click still does at once; the still comes back when the pointer leaves) · chosen, hover and focus from the choice item. A picture arriving, failing or turning never moves the layout.
Sizes
A grid of repeat(auto-fill, minmax(size, 1fr)) with 4 px gaps; the tile is its column wide, the frame square, the label 15 px.
When
Rows whose choices differ in shape (the Character panel's hairstyles). Not for colour-only rows (a swatch) and never a substitute for the 3D view, which stays the true preview.
Combine
The Character panel's creator choices put previewTile({ label, glyph }) in a choiceItem (class preview-choice) inside a .choices.previews[data-size] grid; the row's Segmented S/M/L sits above it (the choiceSize.set UI preference, per feature type).
Adapt
Columns follow the panel's width; tiles use content-visibility: auto, so a 283-choice row costs little until scrolled. Forced colours drop the colour matrix (the raw channels still read as shapes) and use system borders.
Driven by
Presentation only: tile.set(url, none), tile.setSpin(strip, frames), tile.spinnable(on) and tile.setMeta(source, state) from the Character context's read-only previews(option, …) row (choice-preview-service.ts); the picture comes from the preview worker or the host's store, keyed by the resolved winner. The turntable strip (24 frames side by side, frame 0 the still) is drawn only for the choice the list wants turning and set as an image only while it turns.
Keyboard & access
The picture is decorative (alt=""); the choice item keeps its name (the label), its description (maker and prepared state) and the listbox keys, with Up and Down moving by the grid's columns.
Do
Keep one frame per row and the tokens only (plus the V's own colour when tinted, later).
Avoid
Realistic renders dropped into slots, a spinner per tile, a picture that changes the tile's size, an error message inside a tile.
See also
lib-choice-list, lib-choice-layouts, c-creator, f-preview-tokens

Remembered view state

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
What a person folded or opened and where each scroll container was, remembered across reloads: the same rows come back at the top, and a folded section stays folded.
Module
studio-ui/view-state.ts, scroll-anchor.ts · RememberedSet, ScrollMemory, VIEW_KEY, holdScroll, revealInView · General
Anatomy
A view key per foldable control or scroll container (<namespace>:<path> or <namespace>.<path>: character:row:head/hair, expressions.mouth, panel:character) · data-view-key on the elements a scroll position can anchor on · a scroll anchor: the element at the top edge, its clip offset (how many px of it are scrolled past the edge), up to four elements before it and the plain scroll position.
Variants
Folds: GroupSection (its key), the Character panel's headings, rows and author groups, a tree's groups (RememberedSet). Scroll: every panel (panel:<id>, the dock group's body), every TreeView (tree:<label>, virtualised), any container with new ScrollMemory(element, key).
States
nothing stored (the control's default); stored; stored for a control not shown yet (kept until it shows); a restore pending (waiting for its content), exact, fallen back to an element before it, or dropped because the person scrolled first.
Sizes
At most 192 open states per namespace and 512 in all, and 64 scroll anchors; the least recently set go first.
When
Every foldable heading, row or group and every container that scrolls a list people come back to. Transient lists (a menu, a popover) aren't remembered.
Combine
Library components do it themselves; a feature names the keys. Section blocks (section()) and GroupSections carry their key as data-view-key; give rows of your own a data-view-key so the scroll position can come back to them.
Adapt
Resizing never loses the place: a height-only change keeps the scroll position; a width change (the content reflows) puts the anchor from before the resize back at minus its clip offset, through a whole splitter drag or window resize, and not while the person is scrolling. A panel floated, docked or re-laid out restores from the anchor recorded as its old container went. Content that loads later (a catalogue, a tree's rows, mods) is waited for: each change tries the restore again until the anchor is exactly where it was (30 s at most). A missing anchor falls back to the nearest element before it that is still there (an element around it keeps how far it was scrolled past), then to the plain position.
Driven by
Presentation state, never Undo and not part of a saved layout: the workspace's expanded and scroll UI preferences (expanded.set {keys, expanded}, scroll.set {key, anchor}), so a verification workspace keeps its own and every layout shows the same state. Recorded on scroll (debounced), when a container is rebuilt and before the page is hidden.
Keyboard & access
Restoring never moves focus. A wheel, touch, key or pointer press in the container drops a pending restore, so the person's own scrolling always wins. Choosing something in a list never moves the view (holdScroll: what is at the top edge stays there for a moment, whatever the choice rebuilds or focuses); bringing an element into view (revealInView) scrolls only its own container, as little as needed, and never during a restore or hold.
Do
Key by what the element is (its slot, section or item ID), not its position or title that can change.
Avoid
Remembering pixel positions alone; restoring after the person has started scrolling; keys in browser storage outside the workspace.

06

Communicating state

Four kinds of state must stay intelligible: the portable recipe/collection (authored work), the browser workspace (draft autosave, selections, view), immutable SQLite library revisions, and exported files. These patterns keep them apart in words and placement.

Saved versus unsaved

Implemented
Not saved yetSavedUnsaved changesNewer version savedWorking…▲ Your latest changes could not be saved.

Your library has a newer version of this collection (version 5) saved elsewhere; your draft started from version 3. Saving will report a conflict — save a copy or reopen it.

What
One save status (UI-89): the library chip says whether your work is saved in the library (never saved, saved, unsaved changes, or behind a newer version saved elsewhere), and its tooltip says the draft autosaves on this computer. The status bar speaks about the draft's autosave only when it has a problem.
When
Always visible in the header and Presets panel; the Library panel explains the consequence in a sentence.
Combine
Save to library records a new immutable revision; edits made while it runs stay in the draft. Export collection/build plan save first and say so.
Adapt
Header chip hides below 720 px; the Presets panel and status bar keep the information.
Driven by
status.workspace, library.summary().draft.revision vs summaries[].revision.
Avoid
Claiming “unsaved changes” — the application does not yet expose a draft-versus-revision diff (audit API gap A-1). Say what is known.

Undo, recovery and view changes

Implemented
What
Three scopes, named consistently: Undo (Ctrl+Z; per look; content edits, one step per gesture or slider drag), recovery (restore removed preset, recover previous collection draft — separate stacks) and view changes (camera, UV pan/zoom, panels, theme — never undoable, never in recipes). The Character panel has one Undo of its own (UI-81): its buttons and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y anywhere in it but a text box step its creator choices and Clothing in order; the header's Undo and History cover the makeup and say so.
When
Toasts offer the matching scope: “Undo” after layer removal or reset, “Restore” after preset removal, “Undo open” after opening a collection.
Combine
Menus group view commands under their own view heading, after the target's edits. Removal commands say “Undo with Ctrl+Z” or “Restorable from the Presets panel”.
Adapt
The same wording in toasts, menus and the palette at every size.
Driven by
history.undo capability; preset.edit restore; collection.recover; views never enter the look history.

Async work and cancellation

Implemented

Building and verifying Cyberpunk mod files from the current collection. This can take several minutes… A started build can't be cancelled, and closing XF Studio doesn't stop it.

What
Busy states show the application's progress message. Where the server cannot cancel, the UI says so instead of offering a Cancel that lies.
When
Library requests, package Check/Build, imports. Collection edits are paused while a library request runs; layer editing continues during a save.
Combine
Collection edits pause (disabled with a reason) while a library request runs; layer editing continues during a save.
Adapt
Progress lives in the panel that started it and in the status bar.
Driven by
library.summary().busy/progress, request capabilities (cancellable: false in request descriptors).

Disabled with a reason

Implemented
Select a layer before exporting a mask.
What
Every unavailable command explains itself with the application's reason, in the menu pattern (UI-84): an unavailable button stays focusable (aria-disabled) and shows its reason as a tip on focus, hover or tap; menus, palette entries and note lines show it as text.
When
Always. If the application gives no reason, that is an API gap to report, not a reason to hide the command.
Combine
The same reason text appears in every entry point for the same action.
Adapt
Reasons wrap under controls; they are never truncated.
Driven by
capability(...).reason and code (missing_target, busy, limit, invalid_value, incompatible_mode, asset_unavailable, not_ready, needs_input).

Errors and recovery

Implemented
Library

The library has a newer revision of this collection. Your draft is kept.

What
Refusals and errors say what happened, confirm what was kept, and offer the specific recovery: conflicts offer Refresh and Save as copy; invalid imports keep the current draft; failed previews keep the last complete textures and offer Rebuild. A refusal is a warning; only a real failure is an error, with its reference and Report this problem.
When
Any refused dispatch or failed request. Errors never silently retry.
Combine
An error toast and an Activity entry for every failure; the panel that started the request keeps its last error until the next attempt.
Adapt
Toasts cap their width; the Activity log keeps the full text.
Driven by
{ ok:false, code, message } outcomes; conflict and stale_result codes add recovery actions.

Stale results

Implemented
What
A result computed from an earlier snapshot stays visible but is labelled Stale with a prompt to run again.
When
Package results after the draft changes (freshness), Glitter flake measurements after the layer or tier changes.
Combine
Stale results keep their content and add a warning note with the next step.
Adapt
The badge wraps under the title in narrow panels.
Driven by
files.package.freshness, status.glitter[].current.

Gesture transactions

Implemented
What
A pointer drag, wheel burst or slider drag is one transaction: one Undo step on completion; Escape, pointer cancel or focus loss restores the start. The status bar says “Gesture in progress · Esc cancels” or “Adjusting · Esc restores”.
When
Every continuous edit on the head, the UV map or a slider. Moving panels and changing the layout cancels an active viewport gesture first.
Combine
Panel moves cancel an active viewport gesture first so a layout change never commits a half-finished edit.
Adapt
Identical in every layout.
Driven by
previewState().gesture / control.

Terminology

Rule
Preset
One complete look; one choice in the single in-game eye-makeup selector (plus Off).
Layer
One shape with colour, opacity and finish inside a preset. Top of the list = front.
Finish
Matte, Satin, Metallic / foil, Shimmer / pearl, Glitter, Glossy / wet look, Colour-shifting. Satin is shown for the internal “regular”.
Draft
The working collection, autosaved on this computer.
Library · revision
Explicit, immutable SQLite saves (r1, r2…). “Save to library”, never just “Save file”.
Collection file · recipe file · build plan
Portable editable data; a build plan is compiler input — none is a mod.
Mod package · Check · Build
Check lists what can be packaged (no files). Build creates your own mod files and checks them; the result says plainly that they are not tested in game and not installed.
Preview only
A browser look that Build cannot turn into mod files yet.
Preview context
The V's creator options (skin, hair, eyes, brows, piercings, makeup…) and the 3D view's toggles: which V the makeup is shown on, never authoring, a save or a package.
What
User-facing words. Internal identifiers (regular, iridescent, xfas/…) never appear in the UI.
When
All labels, messages and docs.

Accessibility checklist

Rule
What
Text ≥4.5:1 and control boundaries ≥3:1 in both themes; visible focus on everything; every icon-only control named; disabled reasons in text; menus/tabs/lists follow ARIA patterns; live regions for results; reduced motion honoured; forced-colors fallbacks; no information by colour alone.
When
Every change. Verify light and dark at 1600 px and 900 px, keyboard-only.

Rules for new UI work

Rule
  1. Mount through createTrustedStudioBootstrap; views receive only StudioPresentationPort (enforced by tests/studio-ui-boundary.test.ts).
  2. Put validation, Undo, persistence and async policy in an application action first; then build the control, menu entry and palette command on it.
  3. Read with port.editor, library.summary(), previewState() and status while repainting; never mutate what you read; snapshot() clones everything and is for diagnostics.
  4. Show capabilities and reasons from the application; never duplicate limits or eligibility in the view (descriptor ranges drive sliders).
  5. Device adapters own canvases, Three, workers, files and network; the view only rehosts viewports and calls ports.
  6. Every new user-visible capability: action/catalogue entry, capability inventory, boundary test, this guide (pattern + status), both themes, keyboard path.
  7. Record unavoidable exceptions with owner and removal criterion in research/authoring/ui-architecture-boundary.md.
What
How to extend the Studio without re-coupling presentation and core.
When
Every feature. The guide is regenerated by tools/build-style-guide.ts from the same CSS and components; tests fail if it falls out of sync.
